recipes.name: Nước Dùng Phở Bò (Beef Phở Broth)
recipes.flavorProfile: Clear, deep beef broth with charred onion and ginger sweetness and a warm haze of star anise, clove and cinnamon.
recipes.healthBenefit: A long simmer of marrow and knuckle bones with a piece of chuck gives a savory broth that carries some protein and minerals from the meat, with sodium from the salt and fish sauce.

ingredients.prepNote: 2500 g beef marrow and knuckle bones simmered in 5700 ml water, counted as 5700 g home-made beef stock (1 g per ml); the bones themselves are not eaten
lifted out after about 1.5 hours, cooled and sliced thin for the bowls

instructions: Char the onions and ginger over a gas flame or under the broiler for 15 to 20 minutes, turning, until blackened in spots and soft. Cool, rub off the burnt skin, halve the onions and smash the ginger.
Cover the bones with cold water in a large stockpot, bring to a hard boil for 2 to 3 minutes, drain, and rinse the bones and the pot clean.
Return the bones to the pot with 6 quarts (5.7 L) fresh water, bring to a boil, then lower to a bare simmer and skim off the scum for 15 to 20 minutes.
Add the onion, ginger, star anise, cloves, cinnamon, salt, fish sauce, rock sugar and the piece of chuck. Keep at a gentle simmer, never a rolling boil, so the broth stays clear.
After about 1.5 hours lift out the chuck, plunge it into cold water for 10 minutes to stop it darkening, then refrigerate it for slicing.

Simmer the broth 1.5 hours more, about 3 hours in all. Strain through a fine sieve, skim the fat (keep a little for flavor) and taste: it should taste slightly too salty from the spoon, since noodles and garnishes soften it. You should have about 4 quarts (3.8 L).

nutritionHighlights.note: From the chuck simmered in the broth and the gelatin drawn from the knuckle bones.
From the salt and fish sauce; a cup of broth is well seasoned, so the bowl needs no extra salt.

citations.source: Viet World Kitchen (Andrea Nguyen), Beef Pho Noodle Soup

recipes.curationNote: Viet World Kitchen, Beef Pho Noodle Soup for every amount and step; 5 to 6 lb bones, 6 qt water, 2 onions, 4 oz ginger, 5 star anise, 6 cloves, 3-inch cinnamon, 1 1/3 lb chuck, 1 1/2 tbsp salt, 4 tbsp fish sauce, 1 oz rock sugar, makes 4 qt; ours matches.

recipes.name: Nước Dùng Phở Gà (Chicken Phở Broth)
recipes.flavorProfile: Light golden chicken broth, clean and sweet, scented with charred ginger, toasted coriander seed and a little clove.
recipes.healthBenefit: A whole chicken plus backs give a broth with protein and some B vitamins from the meat, lighter in fat than the beef version once skimmed.

ingredients.prepNote: lifted out after 25 minutes; the meat is shredded for the bowls and the bones go back in

ingredients.baseName: Chicken, broiler, back, meat and skin

ingredients.cutPrep: a 4-inch piece, unpeeled, charred and smashed

instructions: Char the onions and ginger over a flame or under the broiler for 15 to 20 minutes until blistered, then peel off the burnt skin and smash the ginger.
Rinse the chicken and backs. Put them in a large pot with 5 quarts (4.7 L) water, bring to a boil, then lower to a gentle simmer and skim for 10 minutes.
Add the onion, ginger, coriander seed, cloves, cilantro stems, salt, fish sauce and rock sugar. Simmer 20 to 25 minutes, then lift out the whole chicken and cool it in cold water.
Pull the breast and thigh meat off the bird, cover and chill it for the bowls, and return the carcass to the pot.
Simmer the broth 1.5 hours more, skimming now and then. Strain, skim most of the fat, and taste for salt. You should have about 16 cups (3.8 L).

nutritionHighlights.note: From the chicken meat and backs simmered in the pot.
Chicken is a good source, and some of it moves into the broth.

citations.source: Viet World Kitchen (Andrea Nguyen), Chicken Pho Noodle Soup

recipes.curationNote: Viet World Kitchen, Chicken Pho Noodle Soup for every amount and step; 4 lb chicken, 3 lb backs, 5 qt water, 2 onions, 4-inch ginger, 1 1/2 tbsp salt, 3 tbsp fish sauce, 1 oz rock sugar, 2 tbsp coriander seed, 4 cloves, cilantro stems, makes 16 cups; ours matches.

recipes.name: Nước Dùng Bún Bò Huế (Huế Beef Noodle Broth)
recipes.flavorProfile: Bold, red, lemongrass-heavy beef and pork broth with the funk of fermented shrimp paste, a little sweetness and a paprika and lemongrass oil.
recipes.healthBenefit: Beef shank and pork hock give the broth protein and collagen, and lemongrass and paprika bring aroma; it is a salty, rich broth best enjoyed as a full meal rather than sipped often.

ingredients.cutPrep: banana shank or brisket, one piece
ingredients.prepNote: lifted out when tender, about 2 to 2.5 hours, and sliced for the bowls

ingredients.cutPrep: hocks, feet or knuckles in small chunks
ingredients.prepNote: lifted out when tender, about 1 hour

ingredients.cutPrep: a quarter of a ripe pineapple, with its core
boneless pork shank, tied with twine
thinly sliced, for the sa tế

ingredients.prepNote: in place of bún bò Huế seasoning mix, as the source allows

instructions: Cover the bones and meat with cold water, boil 5 minutes, drain and rinse every piece and the pot well. Tie the boneless pork shank with twine.
Return everything to the pot with 6 quarts (5.7 L) water, the tied lemongrass, onion, ginger and pineapple. Bring to a boil, then simmer on low, partly covered, skimming as needed.
Lift out the meat as it turns tender: the pork bones after about 1 hour, the pork shank after about 2 hours, the beef shank after about 2.5 hours. Chill and slice for topping.
Remove the aromatics. Whisk the mắm ruốc with a ladle of broth and stir it in, then season with the bouillon powder, fish sauce, salt and rock sugar.
For the sa tế, heat the oil on medium-low, fry the shallot and sliced lemongrass about 10 seconds, add the garlic and paprika for about 5 seconds, take off the heat and stir it all into the broth.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the beef shank and pork bones simmered in the broth.
Fish sauce, shrimp paste and salt make this a well-seasoned broth.

citations.source: Vicky Pham, Vietnamese Spicy Beef Noodle Soup (Bún Bò Huế)

recipes.curationNote: Vicky Pham, Vietnamese Spicy Beef Noodle Soup (Bún Bò Huế) for every amount and step; one pot for 8 bowls, the same 6 quarts of water as ours: 3 lb pork bones (hocks, feet or knuckles), 1 lb boneless pork shank, 1 1/2 lb beef banana shank or brisket, 1/2 lb tendon optional, 4 lemongrass stalks, 10 shallots or 1 large onion, 50 g ginger, 1/4 ripe pineapple with core; 1 tbsp chicken or mushroom bouillon powder, 2 tbsp fish sauce, 2 tbsp sea salt, 2 tbsp mắm ruốc, 20 g rock sugar; sa tế of 1/2 cup oil, 1 shallot, 1/3 cup sliced lemongrass, 3 garlic cloves, 3 tbsp bún bò Huế seasoning mix or paprika.

recipes.name: Nước Dùng Xương Heo (Pork Bone Broth)
recipes.flavorProfile: Mild, clean and slightly sweet pork bone broth, rounded by charred onion and deepened with dried squid and dried shrimp, the everyday base of southern noodle soups.
recipes.healthBenefit: Pork bones and a piece of loin give a light broth with some protein, and the dried squid and shrimp add savory depth.

ingredients.cutPrep: neck and back bones in chunks
ingredients.prepNote: parboiled 3 to 5 minutes and rinsed before the main simmer
lifted out after about 40 minutes and sliced for the bowls

ingredients.baseName: Crustacean, processed shrimp, boiled and dried shrimp

instructions: Cover the pork bones with cold water, boil hard for 3 to 5 minutes, drain, and rinse the bones and pot well.
Char the onion halves cut side down in a dry pan for 4 to 5 minutes until browned.
Return the bones to the pot with 5 quarts (4.7 L) water, bring to a boil, lower to a gentle simmer and skim for 15 minutes.
Add the onion, dried squid, dried shrimp, rock sugar, salt and the pork loin. Lift out the loin after 35 to 45 minutes, when cooked through, and cool it for slicing.
Simmer the broth 1.5 to 2 hours in all, never boiling hard. Strain and taste for salt; it should taste a little strong. You should have about 16 cups (3.8 L).

nutritionHighlights.note: From the pork loin, the pork bones and the dried seafood.

citations.source: Viet World Kitchen (Andrea Nguyen), Hu Tieu Nam Vang

recipes.curationNote: Viet World Kitchen, Hu Tieu Nam Vang for every amount and step; 6 lb pork bones, 5 qt water, 2 oz dried squid, 1/3 cup dried shrimp, 1 onion, 1 oz rock sugar, 2 tbsp salt, 1 1/4 lb pork; makes 4 qt; no daikon or fish sauce.

recipes.name: Nước Dùng Chay (Vegetable Broth)
recipes.flavorProfile: A clear, sweet vegetable broth with charred onion and ginger, kombu and shiitake depth, and the phở spices of star anise and cinnamon.
recipes.healthBenefit: Daikon, carrot, kombu and shiitake make a plant broth with savory depth, low in fat, with a little iodine from the kelp.

ingredients.prepNote: 1 each at 2 g per each; in place of black cardamom pod, which the database does not hold

ingredients.cutPrep: one small daikon, cut in chunks

ingredients.baseName: Japanese radishes, Daikon, root, pickles, "Takuan-zuke" (pickled with rice bran and salt), made of salted Daikon

instructions: Char the onion, shallots and ginger over a flame or in a dry pan for 8 to 10 minutes until blackened in spots, then peel off the burnt skin.
Toast the star anise, cinnamon and black cardamom in a dry pan for 1 to 2 minutes until fragrant, and tie them in a spice bag.
Put everything except the salt and miso in a pot with 3 L water, including the dried garlic and pickled radish, bring to a boil, then simmer gently for 45 minutes to 1 hour.
Strain and season with the salt. Dissolve the miso in half a cup of the hot broth and stir it back in, then taste. You should have about 10 cups (2.4 L).

nutritionHighlights.note: From the kombu simmered in the pot.
From the daikon, carrot and shiitake.

recipes.name: Nước Chấm (Dipping Fish Sauce)
recipes.flavorProfile: Bright, sweet, sour and salty all at once, with garlic and chile bite and a few shreds of carrot.
recipes.healthBenefit: A spoonful dresses a whole bowl of herbs and noodles with little fat; it carries sodium and some sugar, so it is meant to be used by the spoonful.
instructions: Stir the lime juice, sugar and lukewarm water in a bowl until the sugar dissolves.
Add the fish sauce a little at a time and taste: it should be balanced between sour, sweet and salty, slightly strong from the spoon.
Stir in the garlic, chile and carrot and let it sit 15 to 30 minutes before serving. Makes about 1 cup and keeps 3 to 4 days chilled.

nutritionHighlights.note: A little from the fresh lime juice.

citations.source: Viet World Kitchen (Andrea Nguyen), Basic Vietnamese Dipping Sauce (Nuoc Cham)

recipes.curationNote: Andrea Nguyen basic nước chấm: lime, sugar, lukewarm water, fish sauce, garlic, Thai chile and shredded carrot, quantities taken from the middle of her ranges. Makes 1 cup, 16 tablespoons.

recipes.name: Nước Mắm Gừng (Ginger Fish Sauce)
recipes.flavorProfile: Hot with fresh ginger, sweet and salty, with lime and chile; the dip for poached chicken and duck.
recipes.healthBenefit: Fresh ginger brings its warm pungency, and a tablespoon carries mostly sodium and a little sugar.

ingredients.cutPrep: peeled and finely minced or pounded

instructions: Pound or mince the ginger, garlic and chiles to a coarse paste.
Stir the sugar into the warm water until dissolved, then add the fish sauce and lime juice.
Stir in the ginger paste and rest 10 minutes before serving. Makes about 1 cup and keeps 1 week chilled.

citations.source: Runaway Rice, Ginger Fish Sauce (Nuoc Mam Gung)

recipes.curationNote: Runaway Rice nước mắm gừng as written: 2 oz ginger, a garlic clove, warm water, 1/4 cup each sugar and fish sauce, 2 tbsp lime, 2 chiles, 10 minute rest. Single source; it matches the ginger fish sauce served with Cơm Gà and gà luộc everywhere.

recipes.name: Tương Chấm Gỏi Cuốn (Peanut Hoisin Dip)
recipes.flavorProfile: Thick, sweet and savory hoisin and peanut dip with fried garlic and crushed peanuts on top.
recipes.healthBenefit: Peanut butter and peanuts give it protein and mostly unsaturated fat; it is rich and sweet, so a couple of spoonfuls go a long way.
instructions: Warm the oil in a small pot over medium-high heat and fry the garlic for 20 to 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add the water and peanut butter and whisk until smooth.
Stir in the hoisin and simmer on low for 1 to 2 minutes until it just bubbles. Thin with water or simmer longer to reach a thick, pourable dip; it thickens as it cools.
Serve in small bowls topped with the chopped peanuts. Makes about 2 cups.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the peanut butter and toasted peanuts.

citations.source: Vicky Pham, Vietnamese Peanut Dipping Sauce for Spring Rolls (Tương Chấm Gỏi Cuốn)

recipes.name: Đồ Chua (Pickled Carrot and Daikon)
recipes.flavorProfile: Crunchy, sweet-sour matchsticks of carrot and daikon that cut through grilled meat and rich pâté.
recipes.healthBenefit: Carrot brings beta-carotene and daikon some vitamin C, in a crisp pickle that is low in fat; most of the brine sugar stays in the jar.

ingredients.cutPrep: one large carrot, cut in matchsticks
2 tsp for kneading plus 1/2 cup for the brine
ingredients.prepNote: most of the brine sugar is left in the jar

instructions: Toss the carrot and daikon with the salt and 2 teaspoons sugar and knead for about 3 minutes, until the daikon bends without snapping and the liquid pools in the bowl.
Rinse in a colander, press out the water and pack into a jar.
Stir the 1/2 cup sugar into the vinegar and lukewarm water until dissolved, pour it over the vegetables to cover, and let stand at least 1 hour.
Refrigerate. It keeps about 4 weeks; open the jar to let the daikon smell out before serving. Makes about 3 cups.

citations.source: Viet World Kitchen (Andrea Nguyen), Daikon and Carrot Pickle (Do Chua)

recipes.name: Mỡ Hành (Scallion Oil)
recipes.flavorProfile: Glossy, gently sweet scallion oil spooned over grilled meats, broken rice and noodles.
recipes.healthBenefit: Mostly canola oil, so it is a fat for finishing; scallions add a little vitamin K.

ingredients.baseName: Onions, spring or scallions (includes tops and bulb)

instructions: Trim the roots, rinse the scallions, pat them very dry and chop them finely.
Warm the scallions, oil and salt in a small pan over medium heat for 3 to 4 minutes, stirring now and then, until the scallions just wilt and stay bright green.
Pour into a bowl and cool slightly before spooning over food. Makes about 1/2 cup.

citations.source: Runaway Rice, Scallion Oil (Mo Hanh)

recipes.curationNote: Runaway Rice, Scallion Oil (Mo Hanh) for every amount and step; 1 large bunch scallions, 1/4 cup oil, 1/8 tsp salt, makes 1/2 cup; ours matches.

recipes.name: Sa Tế (Lemongrass Chili Oil)
recipes.flavorProfile: Deep red chili oil thick with fried lemongrass and garlic, hot, fragrant and a little sweet.
recipes.healthBenefit: A spoonful adds heat and aroma; chiles and paprika bring carotenoids, and it is mostly oil, so it is used sparingly.

ingredients.cutPrep: two bulbs, cloves smashed and peeled
stalks, tender part sliced and finely ground

instructions: Pulse the lemongrass in a food processor for about 45 seconds, scrape down, add the garlic and pulse another 45 seconds to a fine mince.
Heat the oil in a skillet over medium-high heat, add the mince, sugar and salt, and fry for about 2 minutes, stirring, until fragrant and pale gold.
Take the pan off the heat and cool 3 to 4 minutes, then stir in the chile flakes and paprika so they do not scorch.
Return to low heat for 2 minutes more, then cool completely and store in a jar in the refrigerator for up to 3 months. Makes about 2 cups.

nutritionHighlights.note: Carotenoids from the dried chiles and paprika.

recipes.name: Muối Tiêu Chanh (Salt, Pepper and Lime Dip)
recipes.flavorProfile: Sharp and salty, a pinch of salt and white pepper loosened with lime for dipping chicken, seafood and shaking beef.
recipes.healthBenefit: Lime brings a little vitamin C; the dip is mostly salt, used a pinch at a time.
instructions: Set out the salt, white pepper, lime wedges and chile in separate small dishes, about 2 parts salt to 1 part pepper.
Each diner puts a pinch of salt and pepper in a small saucer, squeezes in a wedge of lime and muddles in chile if they like, then dips each bite just before eating.

recipes.curationNote: Viet World Kitchen, Salt, Pepper and Lime Dipping Sauce for every amount and step; no amounts, only 2 parts salt to 1 part white pepper by volume, a lime squeeze per diner, chile optional.

recipes.name: Nước Màu (Caramel Sauce)
recipes.flavorProfile: Dark, bittersweet caramel used in small amounts to color and deepen braises and grilled marinades.
recipes.healthBenefit: This is sugar cooked dark, used by the teaspoon for color and flavor rather than as a source of nutrients.

ingredients.cutPrep: 3 tbsp for melting the sugar plus 1/4 cup hot water at the end

instructions: Put the sugar and 3 tablespoons water in a medium saucepan over medium heat. In about 3 minutes it melts and bubbles; stir and keep cooking.

Watch it turn golden at about 4 minutes, rich brown at about 6, and deep reddish brown with a little smoke at 7 to 8. Cook 30 to 45 seconds more, then turn off the heat and let it settle for about 10 minutes.
Carefully add the 1/4 cup hot water, return to medium heat and stir until it boils again, then turn off the heat and stir about 1 minute more.
Cool at least 10 minutes and pour into a clean jar. It thickens as it cools and keeps up to a year in a cool, dry place. Makes about 3/4 cup.

citations.source: Runaway Rice, Caramel Sauce (Nuoc Mau)

recipes.curationNote: Runaway Rice nước màu with her minute by minute color cues. Single source; the method is the standard one for nước màu.

recipes.name: Nước Chấm Chay (Vegetarian Dipping Sauce)
recipes.flavorProfile: The sweet, sour and savory balance of nước chấm with soy sauce in place of fish sauce, sharp with lime and chile.
recipes.healthBenefit: A plant-only dipping sauce that keeps vegetarian dishes free of fish; it carries sodium from the soy sauce and some sugar.

ingredients.baseName: Soy sauce made from soy and wheat (shoyu)

instructions: Stir the lime juice, sugar and water until the sugar dissolves.
Add the soy sauce and taste, adjusting until tart, sweet and savory are balanced.
Add the chile and rest about 10 minutes before serving. Makes about 1 cup.

recipes.name: Sốt Mayonnaise Bánh Mì
recipes.flavorProfile: Rich, pale yellow egg yolk mayonnaise, soft and a little tangy, spread thick inside bánh mì.
recipes.healthBenefit: Made from egg yolks and canola oil, it is a rich spread high in fat, much of it unsaturated, used by the spoonful.
instructions: Put the yolks, salt, white pepper, mustard powder, lemon juice and rice vinegar in a large bowl and beat with a hand mixer on low for 10 seconds.
Add 1 tablespoon oil and beat 30 seconds, then raise the mixer to high.
Keep adding oil 1 tablespoon every 30 seconds until it is all in; the sauce thickens around the halfway point and ends thick and creamy.
Refrigerate and use within a week. Makes about 1 cup.

citations.source: Runaway Rice, Mayonnaise
Viet World Kitchen (Andrea Nguyen), Bánh Mì Recipe for Making Vietnamese Sandwiches Anytime

recipes.name: Cơm Trắng (Steamed Jasmine Rice)
recipes.flavorProfile: Fluffy, fragrant jasmine rice with separate, tender grains.
recipes.healthBenefit: Plain steamed rice is an easy-to-digest source of carbohydrate for energy, naturally gluten-free and low in fat.

ingredients.baseName: Grains, rice, white, long-grain, regular, dry

instructions: Rinse the rice in a pot of cool water, swishing, and pour off the cloudy water 2 to 3 times until it runs nearly clear. Drain well.
Add the 600 ml water, bring to a boil over medium-high heat, then lower to a simmer for 1 to 3 minutes until the water drops to the level of the rice.
Cover, turn the heat to low and cook 10 minutes. Turn off the heat and rest 10 minutes covered.
Fluff the rice with a paddle, cover again and rest 10 minutes more before serving. Makes about 6 cups.

citations.source: Viet World Kitchen (Andrea Nguyen), Perfect Jasmine Rice, the 10-10-10 Method

recipes.curationNote: Andrea Nguyen 10-10-10 jasmine rice: 2 cups rice to 2 1/2 cups water, about 6 cups cooked. The database has no jasmine rice row, so long-grain white rice stands in as the same kind of grain.

recipes.name: Xôi Trắng (Steamed Sticky Rice)
recipes.flavorProfile: Chewy, glossy steamed sticky rice, lightly salted, the base for xôi toppings at breakfast.
recipes.healthBenefit: Glutinous rice is a dense source of carbohydrate and is naturally gluten-free despite its name.

ingredients.prepNote: soaked 3 to 8 hours in cold water, then drained

instructions: Rinse the rice until the water runs clear, then soak it in plenty of cold water for at least 3 hours or overnight. Drain well.
Toss the drained rice with the salt. Line a steamer with cheesecloth or a banana leaf if the holes are large, and spread the rice in an even layer.
Steam covered over medium heat for 30 minutes, then fluff and turn the rice and steam 10 to 15 minutes more, until every grain is glossy, translucent and chewy.
Serve warm, pressed into a bowl or wrapped in leaves. Makes about 6 cups.

citations.source: Vicky Pham, Vietnamese Red Sticky Rice (Xôi Gấc)

recipes.curationNote: Vicky Pham, Vietnamese Red Sticky Rice (Xôi Gấc) for every amount and step; 1 1/2 lb glutinous rice with 1/2 tsp sea salt; ours keeps the rice, salt and steaming and leaves out the gac, coconut milk and sugar for plain rice.

recipes.name: Bánh Phở Tươi (Fresh Rice Noodles)
recipes.flavorProfile: Soft, silky and slightly chewy fresh rice noodles, steamed in thin sheets and cut into wide ribbons.
recipes.healthBenefit: Rice flour and starch make a naturally gluten-free noodle that is mostly carbohydrate.
instructions: Whisk the rice flour, tapioca starch, potato starch, salt and water until smooth and rest 30 minutes. Whisk again before every pour, since the starch settles quickly.
Set a shallow bowl in a wide pot with about 2 inches of water, set a 9-inch nonstick cake pan on it, and bring the water to a boil over medium-high heat.
Pour about 1/3 cup batter into the pan, swirl it thin, cover and steam about 2 minutes, until translucent.
Lift the pan out, loosen the sheet with a wooden chopstick and slide it onto an oiled tray. Brush with a little oil and repeat with the rest of the batter.
Stack the cooled sheets and cut them into ribbons about 1/4 to 1/2 inch wide. Use within the day.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the rice flour and starches.

citations.source: Vicky Pham, Vietnamese Steamed Rice Noodle Sheets (Bánh Ướt)

About 4 bowl portions. Single opened source.

recipes.name: Chả Lụa (Vietnamese Pork Roll)
recipes.flavorProfile: Springy, smooth, pale pork roll seasoned with fish sauce and white pepper, with a faint scent of banana leaf.
recipes.healthBenefit: Mostly pork, so it brings protein and B vitamins; it is salty and fairly rich, so a couple of slices is a usual portion.

ingredients.prepNote: plus a little for brushing the leaves

instructions: Whisk the ice water, fish sauce, oil, sugar, potato starch and white pepper, then stir in the baking powder.
Mix the liquid into the pork on low speed for 3 to 4 minutes, spread it thin in a metal pan and chill about 3 hours, until firm but not frozen.
Working in two batches and keeping the meat cold, pulse it in a food processor 10 seconds on and 10 seconds off for about 5 minutes, scraping down, until it is a smooth, sticky paste.
Shape each batch into a log in plastic wrap and chill 20 minutes. Wrap each log snugly in 2 to 3 oiled banana leaves, then in plastic wrap, and tie loosely with twine.
Bring the steamer water to a boil, lower to a gentle steam and steam the rolls 20 to 25 minutes, until firm. Cool 15 to 20 minutes, unwrap and slice. Makes 2 rolls of about 1 lb (450 g).

nutritionHighlights.note: Pork is one of the richest common sources.

citations.source: Runaway Rice, Steamed Pork Roll (Cha Lua / Gio Lua)
Wikipedia, Chả lụa

recipes.curationNote: Runaway Rice chả lụa (giò lụa in the north): 2 lb pork, ice water, fish sauce, oil, sugar, potato starch, white pepper, baking powder, pounded smooth, wrapped in banana leaf and steamed. Wikipedia confirms pork paste seasoned with fish sauce and pepper, wrapped in banana leaves and steamed. 16 slices of about 55 g.

recipes.name: Pa Tê Gan (Liver Pâté)
recipes.flavorProfile: Rich, coarse, savory pork liver pâté with shallot, garlic and five-spice, smooth enough to spread thick on bánh mì.
recipes.healthBenefit: Pork liver makes this rich in vitamin A, iron and B12; it is also rich in fat, and liver is best eaten in small amounts, especially in pregnancy because of its vitamin A.

ingredients.cutPrep: cut in 1 inch pieces, soaked 30 minutes in milk and rinsed

ingredients.baseName: Milk, whole, 3.25% milkfat, with added vitamin D
ingredients.cutPrep: half for the liver, half for the bread
ingredients.prepNote: for soaking the liver and bread; most is poured off

ingredients.cutPrep: half minced for the pork, half kept to lay on top

instructions: Soak the liver in half the milk and the bread in the other half for 30 minutes. Mince the shallots, the garlic and half the pork fat. Drain the liver and rinse it until the water runs clear, and squeeze the milk from the bread.

Heat 1 tbsp oil over medium-high heat, cook half the shallots 30 seconds, then half the garlic 15 seconds, and season with 1/2 tsp salt. Add 1 tbsp butter, the liver and 1/4 tsp five-spice and cook only 15 to 30 seconds, until lightly browned. Take off the heat.

In the same pan heat 1 tbsp oil, cook the rest of the shallots 30 seconds and the rest of the garlic 15 seconds. Add the minced pork fat, ground pork, 1/4 tsp five-spice, 1/2 tsp salt, 1 tbsp butter, the sugar and pepper and cook about 2 minutes until lightly browned.
Blend both mixtures with the bread and the egg until smooth, in batches if needed.

Pour into a buttered, parchment-lined 4.5 by 8 inch loaf pan, lay the remaining pork fat on top and cover tightly with foil. Steam over simmering water 1 to 1 1/4 hours, until a toothpick comes out clean.
Cool to room temperature, then chill at least 2 hours. Lift off the fat before serving.

nutritionHighlights.note: Pork liver is very rich in it.

instructions: Stir the yeast into 1/2 cup of the warm water and let it foam for about 5 minutes.
Pulse the flour, salt and sugar in a food processor, add the yeast and the remaining 1 cup water, and run until a soft dough forms a ball, then 30 to 45 seconds more to knead.
Let the dough rise covered for about 1 hour, until it nearly fills the bowl. Deflate with a pulse or two and let it rise twice more, each time shorter than the last.
Divide into 8 pieces and shape each into a short torpedo about 7 inches long. Proof on a floured sheet for about 30 minutes, until just shy of doubled.

Heat the oven to 450°F (230°C) for 30 minutes with a pan of hot water on the lowest rack. Slash each roll once lengthwise, mist with water and bake in the upper third for 15 to 20 minutes, misting twice in the first 6 minutes, until deep golden and crisp all over.
Cool on a rack. The rolls are best the day they are baked; recrisp in a hot oven for 3 to 5 minutes before filling.

instructions: Slice the beef thin and marinate 10 minutes with a little of the fish sauce and pepper.
Squeeze the pickled mustard greens dry and chop them fine.
Heat the oil over high heat, fry the garlic until fragrant and stir-fry the beef until just cooked.
Add the mustard greens and stir-fry with the beef about 2 minutes.
Add the cold rice and stir well, then add the eggs and stir quickly so they coat the rice.
Season with the rest of the fish sauce and pepper, add the green onion and stir 1 minute more before taking off the heat.

citations.source: Cookpad Vietnam, Cơm Rang Dưa Bò

recipes.curationNote: Cookpad Vietnam, Cơm Rang Dưa Bò for every amount and step; serves 2, doubled to our 4: 400 g cold cooked rice, 150 g beef, 100 g pickled mustard greens, 2 green onion stalks, 1 egg, 1 tsp minced garlic, 2 tbsp oil, 1 tbsp fish sauce, 1/2 tsp black pepper; beef marinated 10 minutes with part of the fish sauce and pepper.
